summary.intent: Run the GSD manager command center to discuss, plan, and execute three UAT gap-closure phases (42 API unpin integrity, 43 FUSE write durability, 44 IPNS conflict handling) for the CipherBox v1.1 milestone.
summary.outcome: Phase 42 fully complete (discuss → plan → 8-plan wave execution → code review → verification → phase.complete). Phase 43 fully executed (4 plans across 4 waves, code review done, verifier found gaps, 4 gap-closure plans created but not yet executed). Phase 44 discussed with CONTEXT.md committed; planning not yet started.

repo: POST /ipfs/unpin uses JwtAuthGuard only — no ownership check; any account holder with a harvested CID can destroy another user's content while victim retains quota debt.

Kubo v0.40 runs with 'server' profile AND swarm port 4001 exposed publicly in staging compose — server profile only disables local-network discovery, DHT participation remains on, so all pinned CIDs are publicly advertised as provider records.
Writable-share saves drop prunedCids without unpinning (shared-write.ts:450), meaning there is no legitimate cross-user unpin path — only the attacker path existed.
BYO unpin was broken in both directions before Phase 42; new guardedUnpin semantics fix server side transparently.

pnpm/jest double-dash gotcha: `pnpm --filter <pkg> test -- --testPathPattern=X` silently breaks — pnpm inserts `--` and jest treats the flag as a positional regex. Correct form: `pnpm --filter <pkg> exec jest --testPathPattern='X'`.

Windows cross-compilation for `cipherbox-fuse --features winfsp` fails on macOS due to pre-existing issues in `windows-future` and `winfsp-sys` registry crates — unrelated to fuse-write-durability changes; validated via `cargo check` instead.
No .prettierignore existed before this session — prettier was silently mangling .planning/ docs and GSD-managed markdown/js files; root cause of VALIDATION.md table breakage.
gsd commit helper (`query commit`) returns `"committed": false` as a false negative even when the commit actually landed — ALWAYS verify via `git log`, never blind-retry.
cleanup-wave helper resolves repoRoot from cwd — must be run from `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box`; running from inside an agent worktree produces false `base_mismatch` errors.

cleanup-wave is not idempotent — aborts the whole run on the first blocked entry; already-merged entries report `branch_mismatch` on rerun. Workaround: write a reduced manifest with only remaining unmerged entries.
node_modules directories and .husky/_ shims in agent worktrees block git merges and must be removed before cleanup-wave runs.

1Password SSH commit signing requires `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` in Bash tool calls; agent errors on signing ('1Password: agent returned an error') require restarting the 1Password app, not retrying indefinitely.

code.finding: Upload-compensation path fires a global pin/rm via ipfsProvider.unpinFile — does not go through guardedUnpin, creating a D-13 race window where compensation can unpin a CID that content-addressed dedup shares with another user.

Kubo v0.40 configured with 'server' profile and swarm port 4001 exposed as tcp+udp. Server profile only suppresses local-network mDNS — public DHT participation remains active, so every pinned CID has a public provider record.
fetchQuota() reconcile added after removeUsage() in deleteFile as a fire-and-forget (.catch(logger.warn)) per Phase 42-02 — fixes quota desync when delete succeeds locally but server state diverges.

guardedUnpin added: pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(cid)) → row delete → refcount → conditional pending_unpins insert → Kubo pin/rm post-commit best-effort. Cross-user attempts emit cipherbox_unpin_cross_user_attempts_total metric and return silent 2XX.
IPFS_PROVIDER provided locally via useFactory to avoid circular import with IpfsModule — same pattern used in pending-unpin.module.ts.
handle_release ordering enforced for D-04/D-05: journal.put(844) → handle.cleanup(892) → reply.ok(894) → spawn(904) → journal.remove-on-success(943). Journal fsync barrier must precede ack to kernel.

handle_mkdir: journal.put(534) placed inside closure before reply.entry(655); conflict arm sends FsEvent::MkdirConflict to re-arm publisher instead of warn-only; journal entry cleared only on parent-publish success per D-11b.

Full rewrite in Phase 43-01: JournalOp enum (UploadFile|MkdirPublish), JournalEntryStatus, JournalEntry, WriteQueue with put/remove/load_all_for_vault/update_status/record_failure/ordered_for_replay. Journal is ciphertext-only (D-06), fsync-before-ack (D-04).

drainPendingUnpins calls provider (not raw Kubo) and error-isolates per row. runDriftReport is strictly read-only — zero .delete( calls in the drift path — outputs NDJSON and publishes gauge metric only.

workflow: When a multi-plan planner agent dies mid-run (socket closed), verify which plan files landed on disk and spawn a continuation planner scoped to only the missing plans — cheaper than re-running from scratch.
Decision coverage gate requires literal 'D-XX:' citation format in plan must_haves sections — grep-based, will fail on paraphrased references.
openapi.json accumulates formatting-only drift as a side-effect of `nest build` — restore with `git checkout --` before merging worktrees to prevent false-positive diffs.
cleanup-wave manifest approach: write a JSON manifest of worktrees before dispatch, remove entries as they merge, write a reduced manifest for rerun if a wave partially fails.
42-05 worktree merge left MERGE_HEAD (all conflicts auto-resolved by git but commit step failed) — conclude with `git commit --no-edit`, then manually remove worktree and branch.
RAM constraint: agent worktrees must only run targeted test patterns, never full monorepo suite — OOM risk is real.
TDD RED gate verification: confirm the RED commit SHA precedes the GREEN commit SHA in git log; presence of test(XX): prefix is not sufficient.
Post-merge gate pattern: API build filter + targeted jest pattern via `pnpm exec jest` (not `pnpm test --`), then schema drift check, then regression gate against prior phase tests.

Independent schema verification via `to_regclass()` query against live Postgres is more reliable than trusting migration runner output — use it as the auto-approve criterion for blocking migration checkpoints.

Rebase phase branches onto completed prior-phase branches before planning to ensure context files are visible with the correct base — `feat/fuse-write-durability` had to be rebased onto completed Phase 42 branch.

friction: 1Password SSH signing failures ('agent returned an error / fatal: failed to write commit object') required user to manually restart the 1Password app mid-session, blocking all commits until recovered.
Planner agent died with socket closed error after writing plans 01-03, requiring filesystem inspection and a manual continuation planner for the remaining plans.
gsd commit helper false negatives (`"committed": false`) caused confusion and wasted retry attempts — blind retries risk creating duplicate commits.
cleanup-wave cwd bug caused false base_mismatch failures when run from the wrong directory; not surfaced in error messaging.
cleanup-wave not being idempotent means a partial merge failure requires manually constructing a reduced manifest file rather than simply re-running.
node_modules and .husky shims inside agent worktrees must be manually removed before each cleanup-wave run — no automatic cleanup.
openapi.json formatting drift from nest build side-effects required `git checkout --` before merges — discovery was reactive, not preventive.
pnpm/jest double-dash forwarding issue is a silent failure — test runs appear to complete but run against wrong files; only caught by noticing wrong test counts.
Two session limit hits required conversation context compaction, with the second requiring a full summary re-injection.
User accidental input ('touring wyatt web bossy') sent twice during wave execution, causing tool rejections that interrupted the orchestrator's response flow.
Phase 43 verifier found gaps requiring 4 additional gap-closure plans — adds unplanned execution work before Phase 43 can be marked complete.
